[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
This profile records an uncertain 1740 birth in Ulster and an uncertain 1801 death in Pennsylvania. The identity bridge between that ancestor and the London defendant described below has not been established.

'''Samuel Glascow'''
* Life archive ID: obpt17610506-1-defend30
* Gender: Male
* Tattoo: No
* First recorded: 6th May 1761

== Criminal Records ==
* Tried: 6th May 1761 at Old Bailey, London
  * Crime: Theft (stealing one bay-colored gelding, value £10)
  * Verdict: Guilty
  * Sentence: Death. A later newspaper reports respite; military commutation remains unverified in the inspected sources.
* Conditional pardon: associated Old Bailey catalogue metadata lists an entry dated 6th May 1761, TNA SP 44/87 f.68; the original document and conditions have not been inspected.
* Sentence respite reported after the royal review of 21st May 1761: the Public Advertiser of Friday 22nd May says the Newgate report was made to the King “Yesterday”. The official respite instrument and pardon conditions remain uninspected.



== Research Notes ==
== Original records and identity limits ==
The [https://www.oldbaileyonline.org/record/t17610506-1 Old Bailey Proceedings, t17610506-1, 6 May 1761] record Samuel Glascow’s gelding-theft indictment, Guilty verdict and death sentence. The owner is William Hayward in the trial. The [https://www.newspapers.com/image/394296948/ Derby Mercury, 22 May 1761, p.3] reports respite, calling the owner Mr Serjeant Heywood. Its adjacent unnatural-crime description applies to Thomas Andrews, not Samuel.

Samuel’s statements about Holbourn work, time abroad and High Wickham residence are attributed defence testimony; the trial supplies no birth date or origin. [https://www.oldbaileyonline.org/record/ar_9141_29053 Associated catalogue metadata] describes a conditional pardon, but does not establish the conditions without its underlying document.

The same case ID, obpt17610506-1-defend30, already appears in the profile’s Digital Panopticon citation. This establishes the case association, not the defendant’s identity with the Ulster/Pennsylvania family. No parent, spouse or descendant relationship is proved by the inspected case or newspaper.

=== Possible Pennsylvania office record ===
[https://www.newspapers.com/image/584905489/ Aurora General Advertiser, 21 September 1791, p.2] lists Samuel Glasgow under Washington among Pennsylvania justices of the peace in commission on 1 September 1791. The original heading and name list were inspected. The same county as this profile’s uncertain later death makes this a possible identity candidate; the record does not prove that this ancestor held the office. Original commission, court, township and signature evidence is still required. This candidate does not bridge the separate 1761 London defendant to the Pennsylvania family.

=== Reported royal-review date ===
The [https://www.newspapers.com/image/34424820/ Public Advertiser, 22 May 1761, p.3] says the report of seven Newgate malefactors was made to the King at St James’s “Yesterday”, and reports Samuel’s respite. A [https://www.newspapers.com/image/34424813/ separate page-1 masthead] is Friday, 22 May 1761, supporting 21 May as the reported royal-review day. This does not verify military commutation or pardon conditions. [https://www.newspapers.com/image/1212389396/ Berrow’s Worcester Journal, 14 May 1761, p.1] reports Samuel among two capital convictions; its manslaughter defendant is William Smith, not Samuel. [https://www.newspapers.com/image/34424864/ Public Advertiser, 26 May 1761, p.4] advertises printed trial proceedings listing Samuel’s horse-stealing case; it is not a new trial. All three original passages were inspected 5 October 2026.

=== Possible Samuel Glascow, Old Bailey defendant ===
The capital-conviction report also appeared in the Derby Mercury on 8 May 1761 and Jackson’s Oxford Journal on 9 May. These are contemporary reports of the same gelding-theft case, rather than separate trials.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/394296692/ The Derby Mercury, 1761-05-08, p.2].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/396510014/ Jackson's Oxford Journal, 1761-05-09, p.2].</ref>

=== Possible Samuel Glasgow, First Maryland Regiment ===
A notice dated Baltimore, 19 October 1777, signed Joseph Ford, orders absent soldiers of the First Maryland Regiment, including Samuel Glasgow, to return by 10 November. It threatens apprehension and punishment as deserters and offers influence toward pardons.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/590968568/ Maryland Gazette, 1777-10-23, p.2].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/41048973/ Maryland Gazette, 1777-11-06, p.2].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/41048937/ Maryland Gazette, 1777-10-23, p.2].</ref>

The printed punctuation does not place Samuel in Captain Murray’s company. The notice names no age, relatives or subsequent service, and its general deserter warning is not an individual finding that Samuel deserted.

This may concern [[Glasgow-3175]]. Uncertain 1740 Ulster birth and 1801 Hanover Township, Washington County death are chronologically compatible. The Washington County context gives a useful officeholder comparison; no land or service identification.

=== Possible Samuel Glasgow, Whitpain boundary landowner ===
Samuel Glasgow is an adjoining landowner in a Whitpain Township execution-sale notice for about fifty acres, late Isaac Williams’s estate, bounded by John Saunders, Samuel Glasgow, John Eldridge and Thomas Blackledge.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/39398014/ The Pennsylvania Gazette, 1770-02-01, p.3].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/39398170/ The Pennsylvania Gazette, 1770-02-15, p.2].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/39401453/ The Pennsylvania Gazette, 1770-08-16, p.3].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/39401610/ The Pennsylvania Gazette, 1770-08-23, p.6].</ref>

Samuel Glasgow is a boundary landowner for thirty acres, part of a fifty-acre Whitpain Township tract, late Isaac Williams’s estate, also bounded by John Saunders and John Eldridge. A sale is advertised for 9 August at William Lawrence’s house in Plymouth Township.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/39400791/ The Pennsylvania Gazette, 1770-07-12, p.3].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/39400983/ The Pennsylvania Gazette, 1770-07-19, p.5].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/39401146/ The Pennsylvania Gazette, 1770-07-26, p.6].</ref>

The two notices concern parts of Isaac Williams’s estate. Being named as an adjoining owner does not establish Samuel’s residence, family or identity with the Maryland soldier or Washington County justice.

This may concern [[Glasgow-3175]]. Uncertain 1740 Ulster birth and 1801 Hanover Township, Washington County death are chronologically compatible. The Washington County context gives a useful officeholder comparison; no land or service identification.
